source: Robert Steven Bianchi, The hydreion of Osiris, ENiM 19 (2026), pp. 177-195, published 25 August 2026
scope: Control for distinguishing sacred water, a vessel representing or mediating Osiris, and a container claimed to hold an anatomical relic.
finding: Recent scholarship re-examines pharaonic and later evidence for water rituals, Osiris/Sarapis, cultic vessels and the Nile inundation. The hydreion class shows that a vessel can be specifically Osirian because of sacred water and cultic representation without being a reliquary containing biological material.
impact: Strengthens container-versus-content controls for Osiris Shaft, Biggeh, Ehnasya and other water-linked Osirian contexts.
Prevents promotion of canopic/Osiris-vase/hydreion-like objects into anatomical-relic candidates without sealed contents, material analysis and provenance.
canonical_seal: WATER CAN REPRESENT OSIRIS WITHOUT CONTAINING OSIRIS.
